[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Container Storage Interface (CSI) Architecture in Kubernetes"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Container Storage Interface (CSI) is a standard that exposes arbitrary block and file storage systems to containerized workloads on Kubernetes. Before CSI, storage volume plugins were tightly coupled with the core Kubernetes codebase, making it difficult to add new storage backends and introducing potential stability risks."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Architecture Concepts"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A CSI plugin consists of two main components running within your cluster: the CSI Controller and the CSI Node plugin. Understanding how they interact with Kubernetes control plane components is crucial for managing stateful applications."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"CSI Controller: Manages the lifecycle of volumes (creation, deletion, attachment, and snapshotting). It typically runs as a Deployment."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"CSI Node: Handles mounting and unmounting of volumes on the specific worker node where the workload is scheduled. It runs as a DaemonSet on every node."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Sidecar Containers"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kubernetes provides a set of standard sidecar containers that communicate with the CSI controller and the Kubernetes API server. These sidecars abstract away the complexity of watching API objects and trigger the corresponding gRPC calls to the CSI plugin."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"external-provisioner: Watches PersistentVolumeClaim objects and triggers CreateVolume and DeleteVolume gRPC calls."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"external-attacher: Watches VolumeAttachment objects and triggers ControllerPublishVolume and ControllerUnpublishVolume gRPC calls."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"node-driver-registrar: Registers the CSI driver with the kubelet on each node using the kubelet plugin registration mechanism."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Example: CSI StorageClass Definition"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: csi-ebs-sc
provisioner: ebs.csi.aws.com
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
parameters:
  type: gp3"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Volume Workflow"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"When a user creates a PersistentVolumeClaim (PVC), the workflow proceeds through several distinct phases. First, the external-provisioner detects the PVC and calls the CSI controller to provision the actual storage backend. Once provisioned, a PersistentVolume (PV) object is created in Kubernetes."},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, when a Pod references the PVC, the scheduler selects a node. The external-attacher then instructs the CSI controller to attach the volume to that specific node. Finally, the local kubelet and the CSI node plugin execute the NodeStageVolume and NodePublishVolume operations to mount the filesystem into the container."}]
